_comment: The root capability, minted on HOST A only. Rung 4's record, unchanged.
It is unchanged deliberately. Rung 5a does not add authority and does not take any
away; it moves the second hop to another machine and asks what survives the trip.
The answer the demo produces is that the capability survives because host A's
capability authority attenuates it before it leaves and host B's refuses to import
anything wider than the receiving service's role -- and that the ORIGIN survives
because the sending sentry stamped it, exactly as it does single-host.
Host B has no copy of this record and never sees it. It sees the narrowed result
of one delegation, asserted by a host it enrolled. See common/chaind/chaind.py,
op "import", which logs that basis on every call.
Still hand-written, and still the largest assumption in the ladder. Rung 5a does
not improve on that; it multiplies it by the number of hosts.
